channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: British Pound loses ground as markets brace for Fed, BoE monetary decisions
item.description: GBP/USD extends its decline on Monday and trades around 1.3470 at the time of writing, down 0.38% on the day. The pair falls to the lower end of its monthly range, weighed down by renewed demand for the US Dollar (USD) ahead of several major monetary policy decisions.

item.title: Brent: Covert tanker flows may ease supply pressure - Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s FX Research team, including Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao, highlight that Brent crude has surged on Strait of Hormuz hostilities but see scope for gradual de-escalation in coming months.

item.title: Euro: ECB credibility may offer support against Dollar – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s Philip Wee argues that the Euro has a subtle advantage over the Dollar this week, as the European Central Bank’s recent hikes and focus on inflation underscore its institutional credibility.

item.title: Gold: CTA liquidation and dip-buying narrative – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay and Bart Melek highlight that CTAs (Commodity Trading Advisors) have turned large sellers of Gold, liquidating nearly half of their net-long exposure as markets price a Federal Reserve hike and higher energy costs.

item.title: Canadian Dollar remains under pressure following mixed inflation data
item.description: USD/CAD edges higher for the fourth consecutive day on Monday as a stronger US Dollar (USD) outweighs support for the Canadian Dollar (CAD) from rising Oil prices. Traders show a muted reaction to the latest Canadian inflation figures.

item.title: Sweden: Election uncertainty and fiscal stance – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s Global Markets Research team, led by Josie Anderson, George Buckley and Andrzej Szczepaniak, notes that Sweden’s 13 September election remains too close to call, with the centre-left only narrowly ahead.

item.title: Gold starts the week lower as traders await Fed verdict
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) kicks off the week on a bearish note as Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike expectations dominate market sentiment ahead of the two-day monetary policy meeting starting on Tuesday.

item.title: Breaking: Canada hedline CPI rose 3.0% YoY in August
item.description: Canada’s inflation held its pace in August, with the headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising 3.0% from a year earlier, matching market expectations and unchanged from the 3.0% increase recorded in July. On a monthly basis, prices declined by 0.1%.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Inflation keeps pressure on – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank economists note that August US CPI data were broadly in line with expectations but still too high for the Federal Reserve. They stress excessive underlying price pressure and say the Fed has already signaled readiness to hike.

item.title: Oil: Geopolitical supply risks tilt bias higher – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategist Christopher Wong says oil risks have risen again as disruptions to Saudi export infrastructure and renewed concerns around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb keep supply risks elevated.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Head-and-shoulders neckline comes under pressure
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades under pressure at the start of the week, with both the fundamental and technical backdrop pointing to further downside. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $63, down roughly 2.40% on the day.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar extends losses as US Dollar strengthens on Fed bets
item.description: NZD/USD extends its decline on Monday, trading around 0.5770 at the time of writing, down 0.72% on the day.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy-regime shift backs JPY against US Dollar – DBS
item.description: Philip Wee at DBS Group Research highlights a growing policy-regime change advantage for the Japanese Yen (JPY) versus the US Dollar (USD). Following joint US-Japan intervention and expectations of further Bank of Japan (BoJ) tightening, speculators have unwound short JPY positions.

item.title: British Pound: BoE hold, slower QT and dovish repricing risk – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad expects the Bank of England (BoE) to keep its policy rate at 3.75% with a likely 6–3 vote, as easing United Kingdom (UK) wage and services inflation allow a pause.

item.title: Japanese Yen trims gains with Fed and BoJ decisions looming
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) holds moderate losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, but remains close to seven-month highs, following a 4% rally in the previous two weeks.

item.title: Indian Rupee likely extends previous week’s downfall on Tuesday
item.description: The Indian Rupee is expected to extend its previous week’s plunge against the US Dollar (USD) after a long weekend on Tuesday. Indian financial markets across equity, commodity and currency remains closed on Monday due to Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations.

item.title: Czech Koruna: Dovish CNB may weaken CZK against Euro - ING
item.description: ING strategist Frantisek Taborsky outlines a busy Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) data calendar but stresses that the Czech National Bank (CNB) meeting is the key event. He expects rates to stay at 3.75% with dovish guidance, contrasting with still-hawkish market pricing.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Rate hike path and data support – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Jim Reid and team say the Fed’s decision on Wednesday is the main market event, with their economists expecting a 25bp hike to 3.75%-4.00% and now forecasting 75bps of hikes over the next seven months.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed hike expectations and limited gains – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes that the US Dollar (USD) has strengthened only modestly even as markets price in a Fed rate hike at this week’s FOMC meeting.

item.title: ECB’s Schnabel: Recent energy-price developments have been quite concerning
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said recent energy-price developments have been "quite concerning" as officials consider further interest-rate increases after last week’s move, Bloomberg reported.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Aussie bears aim for a key support area around 0.7110
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) resumed its downtrend against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, weighed by the risk-off market mood, as Oil prices consolidate above $100, and rising bets that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will hike interest rates on Wednesday.

item.title: Brent jumps above $104 as fresh supply threats rattle Oil markets
item.description: Brent Oil gains on Monday and trades around $104.20 at the time of writing, up 2.49% on the day. Oil prices benefit from a renewed geopolitical risk premium as tensions in the Middle East revive concerns over potential disruptions to energy supplies.

item.title: Fed to raise interest rates to 3.75%-4.00% on September 16 – Reuters poll
item.description: According to a Reuters poll, the survey on September 9 showed that 86 of 101 economists expect the Federal Reserve (Fed) to hike interest rates by 25 basis points (bps) to 3.75%-4.00% on September 16. This is a dramatic shift from 65 of 93 economists expecting a hold in the previous poll.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: US Dollar gains momentum and targets 1.3940 area
item.description: US Dollar (USD) appreciates for the fourth consecutive day against the Canadian Dollar (CAD) on Monday, as rising bets of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike on Wednesday offset the traditional positive impact of higher Oil prices on the Canadian Dollar.

item.title: British Pound: Downside pressure persists against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang notes GBP/USD rebounded from 1.3479 to close at 1.3535 after an overdone drop, with intraday price action expected to consolidate between 1.3485 and 1.3540.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ guidance crucial for further gains against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategist Christopher Wong notes that JPY has extended gains, pushing USD/JPY near recent lows despite firmer Fed hike pricing and higher US front-end yields. Markets are positioned for a 25bp Bank of Japan (BoJ) hike, with speculative positioning now net long JPY.

item.title: WTI extend opening gains amid fears of further energy supply risks
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, extends its opening gains in the European trading session on Monday, trading almost 3% higher slightly above $99.50.

item.title: Swiss Franc nears yearly lows as Fed rate hike bets boost US Dollar
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) keeps trading lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, as investors brace for a quarter-point interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve (Fed) later in the week, and Oil prices consolidate above $100.00.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Monday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $63.22 per troy ounce, down 2.14% from the $64.60 it cost on Friday.

item.title: Brent: Supply risks keep prices elevated – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Bank’s Danske Research Team highlights a sharp move higher in Brent as escalating Middle East tensions threaten key supply routes. The report notes Brent’s jump above USD 107/bbl and warns that closure of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline could endanger up to 4% of global Oil supply.
